sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from FY2017 to FY2026, from $37.8 billion to $67.4 billion [F196][F1][F10].
Operating margin dropped 11.8pp to 25.7% in FY2022 [D246][F30], which the filing attributes mainly to litigation charges in operating expenses [P58].
The FY2023 step-up was 17.7% revenue growth [D280], which management attributed to contributions from the Cerner acquisition [P48].
The window is a step-up pattern rather than steady compounding, and margins have since recovered.
Cloud Infrastructure supplied 84% of constant-currency cloud growth in FY2026 [P17], adding 13.7pp [D645] to revenue growth of 17.3% [D421].
Cloud Applications added 2.8pp [D668] on a 23.6% revenue share [D666], about a fifth of the Cloud Infrastructure contribution [D645].
Software License fell 8.9% [D681], subtracting 0.8pp [D682] from growth as a shrinking legacy line.
Operating income rose 16.6% [D422] while revenue rose 17.3% [D421], so operating costs grew faster, by 17.7% [D436].
Incremental margin fell to 29.4% [D442] from 52.4% in FY2025 [D395], showing weaker operating leverage.
Operating margin of 30.6% [F34] is below the 32.2% window median [D788] and the 37.6% high [D787].
Operating expenses rose $7.0 billion, led by $6.0 billion more cloud and software costs, mainly infrastructure [P19], and $1.5 billion of restructuring [P11].
The FY2026 bridge shows R&D adding 1.9pp [D444] while other cost lines took 2.1pp [D445].
The largest move, FY2022's 11.8pp fall [D246], came mainly from other cost lines (-11.0pp) [D259], which the filing ties to litigation charges [P58].
Stock-compensation tax benefits of $1.5 billion largely offset a $933 million remeasurement charge [P9], and the effective tax rate was 28.4% [D407] against 39.2% [D360].
Operating cash flow was $32.0 billion, or 1.88x net income [F84][D408], but free cash flow was -$23.7 billion, or -1.39x net income [F104][D409].
Capital expenditure rose $34.4 billion [P5] to $55.7 billion [F94], or 82.6% of revenue [D404] against 37.0% in FY2025 [D357].
The $11.2 billion operating cash flow increase included $4.6 billion of customer prepayment inflows [P6].
Cash conversion now depends on how fast capital spending slows, not on earnings.
Net debt widened to $97.6 billion from $81.4 billion, or -145.0% of revenue [D414][D367][D415].
That ranks at the 0th percentile among six software peers [D815], against a peer median of -0.5% [D816].
Working capital turned positive to $4.8 billion [F174], mainly from financing proceeds including $42.7 billion of senior notes [P8].
Dividends of $5.8 billion [X165] and buybacks of $95 million [X155] compare with free cash flow of -$23.7 billion [F104], and diluted shares rose 1.7% [D438].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion [D412] cover 1.3 years of the $23.7 billion burn [D419][D418], the highest-severity flag [R1].
Free cash flow was below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026 [D362][D409], two years running [R2].
FY2026 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and rounded; the 10-K figure is $17.1 billion against $17.0 billion [X20][F44][R5].
Capex at 82.6% of revenue [D404] compares with 37.0% in FY2025 [D357]; a fall below 37.0% in the FY2027 10-K would show spending easing.
Cash and investments cover 1.3 years of burn [D419]; a cover below 1.3 years in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the funding gap is widening.
Operating margin of 30.6% [F34] compares with the 32.2% median [D788]; a return above the median in the FY2027 10-K would show cloud scale offsetting infrastructure costs.
